# visionary_dashboard (Resource)

A custom dashboard: saved and built-in panels on a 12-column grid, with optional variables and its own time range.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "visionary_dashboard" "checkout" {
  name        = "Checkout"
  description = "Latency, errors and traffic of the checkout service"

  # Built-in charts by ref (overview/…, performance/…, system/…), or a saved
  # panel by its id with kind = "saved". The grid is 12 columns wide.
  panels = jsonencode([
    { id = "latency", kind = "builtin", ref = "overview/latency", x = 0, y = 0, w = 6, h = 4 },
    { id = "errors", kind = "builtin", ref = "overview/error_rate", x = 6, y = 0, w = 6, h = 4 },
    { id = "traffic", kind = "builtin", ref = "overview/traffic", x = 0, y = 4, w = 12, h = 4, title = "Requests" },
  ])

  variables = [{ name = "service", default = "checkout" }]
  time      = { kind = "relative", key = "24h" }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name.
- `panels` (String) The panels as a JSON array, best written with jsonencode(). Each has id, kind (saved or builtin), ref (a saved panel id, or a built-in chart such as overview/latency), x, y, w, h on the 12-column grid, and optionally title, description, params, field and viz. Formatting and empty fields don't count as changes.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description.
- `time` (Attributes) A time range of its own instead of the global one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--time))
- `variables` (Attributes List) Variables shown above the panels. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--variables))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The id Visionary gave it.

<a id="nestedatt--time"></a>
### Nested Schema for `time`

Required:

- `kind` (String) relative or absolute.

Optional:

- `from` (String) Absolute range start, RFC 3339.
- `key` (String) Relative range: 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d or 30d.
- `to` (String) Absolute range end, RFC 3339.


<a id="nestedatt--variables"></a>
### Nested Schema for `variables`

Required:

- `name` (String) instance, route or service.

Optional:

- `default` (String) Starting value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the number Visionary shows, for example in the API.
terraform import visionary_dashboard.example 12
```
